attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post. He stresses them himself in the next line.

semantics.note: Firm 'will not' language makes this a forecast. The proposition keeps the few-months horizon on the Altman clause and leaves the Microsoft/Google clause without a deadline.

contract.note: 'Makes me eat crow' and 'worth it' are subjective, and the speaker gave no standard for either. The contract is right not to invent one. Any pass/fail result would depend on an interpretation the speaker did not give.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own announcement of o1, dated 12 Sep 2024, about two months after the post. It shows a release happened, not that it met either subjective test.

reviews.rationale: The few-months window has passed. But whether any release made the author 'eat crow', or made the spending 'worth it', has no testable standard. The o1 release is context only. With no agreed criterion the claim cannot be scored either way.

attribution.note: He sums up Covello's view in his own voice ('In plain English') and repeats it as his own a few lines later. That counts as endorsed.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps both the claimed effect (no money for anybody) and the stated cause (no extra money for companies that adopt it).

contract.note: The plain reading of 'isn't making any money for anybody' takes its absolute wording literally, so sellers of AI products and infrastructure count. That is an ordinary reading. Narrowing it to firms that adopt the tech would go against 'anybody'. The cause clause was not tested.

evidence.note: Nvidia earned $14.9B of GAAP net income in the quarter ending April 2024, inside the target period. This is a news report of the company's results.
Nvidia's CEO credits generative AI demand for the record data center growth. This is the company's own attribution, which is what the contract's measurement rule asks for.
Microsoft said AI added 7 points to Azure's growth in the January–March 2024 quarter. That is AI revenue to a provider, though measured as growth points, not dollars.

reviews.rationale: The claimed effect, that generative AI was making no money for anybody, is false in the first half of 2024. Nvidia reported large profits, which it put down to generative AI demand, and Microsoft reported AI revenue in Azure. A causal claim fails when its effect is false. The stated cause, adopters gaining no extra revenue, was not separately tested.

attribution.note: His own summary ('In essence') in his own post. It draws on the Goldman report but is stated as his view.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps every listed absence. Leaving out the power-grid clause is fine because that is a separate assertion.

contract.note: 'Not generating any revenue' is firm and literal, so any substantial revenue contradicts it. Scoring the joined claim as false when a firm part is clearly false is fair. 'Killer app', 'meaningfully' and 'massively' are vague and remain unresolved.

evidence.note: Bloomberg reported a $3.4B annual revenue pace for OpenAI in June 2024, citing a source on Altman's remarks to staff. It is a run rate, but it is clearly well above zero.
Microsoft reported AI revenue contributing 7 points of Azure growth in the January–March 2024 quarter.
Nvidia put its record $22.6B data center quarter, ending April 2024, down to generative AI demand. That is infrastructure revenue, which falls within the contract's scope.

reviews.rationale: The claim that generative AI was generating no revenue is clearly false for the first half of 2024: OpenAI, Microsoft and Nvidia all had substantial revenue tied to it. Under the contract's rule for joined claims, that makes the whole claim false. The packet does not settle the productivity, GDP, jobs or killer-app parts.

attribution.note: His own argument in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition captures the 'cannot be trained' assertion but leaves out its stated reason, that these qualities come from lived experience. It is broadly faithful, but it is really a philosophical claim and cannot be tested.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no fair test. 'These' bundles behaviour, responsibility and lived experience, and the claim does not say whether it means a current limit or an inherent impossibility.

evidence.note: A March 2024 preprint on ChatGPT as a co-designer of games. It reports both benefits and shortcomings and does not address whether these qualities can be trained or about responsibility.

reviews.rationale: The claim mixes observable creative ability with responsibility and human experience, and asserts an impossibility without a measurable standard. No empirical result can fairly support or contradict it as written, and the preprint is context only.
